rule: A clearance_iv or vss value is human in-vivo intravenous PK only if every ChEMBL activity behind it comes from an organism-based assay (bao_format BAO_0000218) in Homo sapiens with no cell type or subcellular fraction and no in-vitro wording (microsomes, hepatocytes, S9, intrinsic clearance, metabolic stability); for clearance, the assay must be total body clearance, not an organ-partial clearance (assay_tissue set, or hepatic/renal/biliary clearance); for vss, the assay must not be an unbound volume; and the assay must not state a non-intravenous route (po, oral, im, sc and similar) without also stating iv. A source document outside the curated human PK compilations listed in scripts/v2_pk.py is accepted only if its PubMed title names the drug as a whole word, carries a human or in-vivo PK term, and does not describe analogues, derivatives, a compound series, synthesis or lead optimisation, a drug-drug interaction, a non-human species or an in-vitro system. Activities failing any test are removed. A field with no valid activity left is dropped (set to null); a field with some valid activities left is recomputed from those alone with the original aggregation (geometric mean within a document, median across documents, censored values ignored). The rule concerns source type only and is applied identically to every drug.
